_comment: Prototype: 'repo publishes a stable GitHub Release matching a tag pattern by a deadline'. Public unauthenticated REST (60 req/h/IP: rate limit => COULDNT_CHECK, never NO).
claim: GitHub repository id 65600975 (pytorch/pytorch) publishes a non-draft, non-prerelease GitHub Release whose tag fully matches the pattern v2\.15\.\d+ with published_at between 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z and 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z.

elements.q: Do the exhibits show a GitHub Release object in repository id 65600975 with tag fully matching the pattern v2\.15\.\d+, draft=false, prerelease=false and published_at on or after 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z and on or before 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z?

custom_definitions: 'Release' means a GitHub Release object returned by the releases endpoint. A git tag with no Release object, a draft, or a prerelease does not count.
The clock is published_at. created_at is the date of the tagged commit/draft creation and is never used (the two differ by hours or days on real releases).

The repository is pinned by numeric id (repo_pin); a repository renamed or transferred keeps its id and is still the one checked, and a new repository that later takes the old name is a different repository and is never checked.
Tag matching is a full-string match of the tag_name against the pattern in the claim; v2.15.0-rc1 and v2.15.0.dev1 do not match.
A release deleted or re-created after publication still counts if a keeper snapshot taken inside the window shows it (RETRACTION_V1).
Early resolution: YES may be declared at the first qualifying release; NO only at/after the deadline, and only from a complete (short-page) release list.
Fallback: if the REST API is blocked or rate-limited the resolver reports COULDNT_CHECK and retries on the recovery ladder; the releases.atom feed or a keeper snapshot may then be used.
Burden of proof is on YES: an unproven or ambiguous release resolves NO.
